gaps.note: the hardware numbers every port - numerals on the SFP56 blocks' teal strips, a pair on the pale strip under each QSFP28 block, one on the blue bar above each QSFP-DD cage - and none of them is legible. The only front image is 649 px wide for a 440 mm panel, so a numeral is three or four pixels tall, and there is no hardware installation guide to carry a Port Overview table. rel-pos is therefore positional within each family and no numerals are printed on the drawing. The datasheet's '40-port' phrasing hints at a single 0-39 range; where it starts is not stated and is not assumed here.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-40DG hardware installation guide's port overview table, or a straight-on photograph of the front panel at 8 px/mm or better.

gaps.note: every jack and lamp block on the left of the front panel is labelled on the hardware, and only 'S9620-40DG' can be read from the flat render. The isometric render adds 'ToD', 'BITS', 'GNSS ANT', '10MHZ' and '1PPS'; the six names in the status-lamp legend strip, the mark under the OOB jack and the two labels on the console/USB block stay illegible. The strings printed as MGMT, CONSOLE and USB in silkscreen[] are the datasheet's names for those interfaces placed where the real ink is, NOT transcriptions of the artwork.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the left end of the front panel, or the hardware installation guide's front-panel figure.

gaps.note: there is no hardware installation guide for this platform, so there is no front-panel LED table, no PSU FRU LED table and no fan FRU LED table. All 62 lamps in this model - six system lamps, 24 SFP56 arrows, 24 QSFP28 arrows and eight QSFP-DD dots - carry a position and a colour taken from the render and no states at all. The S9510-28DC and S9321-64E tables in this library belong to other platforms and are not transferable.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-40DG hardware installation guide's LED sections, or a NOS LED table.

gaps.note: a small ROUND RECESSED FEATURE sits alone at the right-hand end of the front panel, centred about (425.1, 33.5), about 2.7 mm across with a bright rim and a dark core, and a printed legend line of four or five characters immediately above it. The feature is drawn as decor because its shape is resolved in both the flat and the isometric render; the legend is not printed because it does not resolve, and the control for that reading is the rest of this panel - no legend resolves in the flat render at all. Nothing in the datasheet mentions anything at that position, so the feature has no identity here: a reset pinhole and an ESD jack are both conventional and neither is sourced. An earlier revision of this file read the same pixels as a warning triangle with no hardware, and printed a triangle in silkscreen; that has been removed.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the right-hand end of the front panel at 8 px/mm or better, or the hardware installation guide's front-panel callout list.

gaps.note: both vendor renders show the AC build, so ufispace/psu-102-ac's face is measured and ufispace/psu-102-dc's is not. The DC unit shares the AC unit's envelope because it seats in the same bay, which is mechanical certainty; everything on its face - the terminal block above all - is drawn on the pattern of ufispace/psu-401-dc and is an estimate. The two must not be read as equally sourced.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on drawing or photograph of the PSU-102-DISB-1 face.

gaps.note: the AC supply's inlet frame measures 23.0 wide by 30.1 tall where a C14 flange is 28 x 20, so the connector is mounted on its side. Which of the two quarter turns it is - earth pin up or earth pin down - is not resolvable at 1.47 px/mm and the component's rotate: 90 is a coin toss between two placements that render identically at this scale.
gaps.wanted: a close photograph of the PSU-102-AISB-1 inlet.

gaps.note: each fan module's flange prints 'FAN <n' and the five read 0 to 4 left to right, but that is per-position printing on a shared component, which no single skin can carry, so nothing on the drawing ties bay 2 to the digit 2. Whether the chassis also prints a digit behind each module cannot be told from an elevation in which the modules cover whatever is behind them.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear with one or more fan modules removed.

gaps.note: the datasheet names FAN-40802825-HD only as an ordering line with no wattage, and gives the two supplies as ratings (1000 W each) rather than draws. There is no installation guide to carry a per-FRU appendix. L27/L29 stand as the live record that the chassis module total is a floor rather than a total, and the device's own 268 W is the vendor's typical figure for a bare box and must not be reconciled against it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-40DG hardware installation guide, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.

gaps.note: no orthographic view of the top, bottom or either side exists. The intake holds a front elevation, a rear elevation and one front-left isometric; the isometric shows the top cover's stampings and a field of holes down the left side, but at 30 degrees on a 250 mm-deep box nothing on those faces can be placed along the depth axis to better than a centimetre. The four views carry their datasheet sizes and nothing else, which holds the device at capability level 2.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-40DG hardware installation guide's dimension drawings, or straight-on photographs of the top and sides.

gaps.note: the four QSFP-DD cages are bracketed in two pairs by a painted orange U. The datasheet says '4 x 400G or 2 x 800G QSFP-DD ports', which makes a pairing the obvious reading, but no document connects the paint to the port modes and the brackets are drawn as decor with no meaning attached.
gaps.wanted: the hardware installation guide's port overview, or a NOS port-mode table.

provenance.attrs: datasheet Specifications (Physical, Environmental, Performance, Regulatory Compliance) and Supported Accessories, all read off the rendered pages because the embedded text is outlined - see provenance.sources. The two memory rows are the vendor's own Standard and Premium builds and both are carried, because dropping either would turn an ordering choice into a fact. Compliance is transcribed as printed and not tidied.
provenance.chassis: datasheet Physical / Chassis (WxDxH): '2RU, 440mm(W) x 250mm(D) x 89mm(H) or 17.32" x 9.84" x 3.50"', 'Weight: 8.5 kg (without FRU)'. 440 IS THE BODY, NOT THE RACK FACE: it is 42 mm inside the 482.6 of a 19-inch opening, the datasheet calls it the chassis rather than the rack width, and both renders show small tabs projecting about 3.5 mm beyond the body at mid-height on each side - mounting furniture, not the 21 mm flanges a 19-inch ear would need. Those tabs are not drawn, per the house rule that ears never are. 89 mm is 0.1 mm over the 88.9 of 2 RU, which is the vendor rounding.
provenance.dd-brackets: measured - each PAIR of QSFP-DD cages sits inside a bright orange U, drawn open at the top where the blue label bars are. Bracket A runs x 370-449 px and bracket B x 458-537, both y 33-54 px: legs about 2.7 mm wide and a bottom bar about 2 mm deep, i.e. 250.86-304.42 mm and 310.52-364.09 mm horizontally, 22.59-36.97 vertically. It is PAINT ON THE PANEL and is drawn as panel.decor, not as a part: it has no identity a part number could be put to, it spans two ports, and the port lamps sit outside it. Why the vendor brackets them in pairs is not stated anywhere; the datasheet's '4 x 400G or 2 x 800G' is the obvious guess and is not written down as a fact. THIS PARAGRAPH WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE BRACKETS WERE DRAWN AND FOR A WHILE DESCRIBED SOMETHING THE FILE DID NOT CONTAIN. The six decor rects that build the two Us - two legs and a bottom bar each - were added afterwards from the numbers above, which are unchanged. Anyone auditing this file should note the failure mode rather than only the fix: sourced provenance for a feature is not evidence that the feature was drawn, and nothing in lint, the render or the name audit could tell the two apart. THE U IS BUILT AS THREE RECTS, NOT AS ONE OUTLINE, so it needs no knowledge of the panel colour to cut its own middle out. The right-hand leg of each U overlaps its cage's registry opening by 0.56 mm, because the aperture the render shades is narrower than the SFF-8665 opening std/qsfp-dd is dimensioned to - the same 1.3 mm effect already recorded for the QSFP28 shells in port-grid. Decor is painted behind the ports, so the cage covers the overlap and the visible leg is 2.14 mm on that side against 2.70 on the other; the measured outer extents are kept rather than nudged into symmetry. COLOUR: the U is the only orange on the device and is nothing like the '#b0b5bb' of the ganged shells elsewhere on this panel - a warning worth keeping, because the treatment was nearly copied across from the SFP blocks instead of being looked at. In s9620-40dg-2-front.png the lit face of the paint is modal (188,118,39) = '#bc7627' with a shadowed side at '#8b551b' and a highlight to (253,154,40); the file carries '#e2821f', the lit face brightened, which is the same treatment the teal port strips ((42,153,129) measured, '#1f9e7a' written) and the QSFP-DD label bars ((71,130,188) measured, '#2f6fd0' written) already had in this file. That is a rendering choice and is recorded as one.
provenance.front-image: photo-measured - the front geometry rests on ONE raster, the 649 x 130 px picture embedded on page 1 of the datasheet (pdfimages object 755). The same drawing appears twice more at lower resolution - 510 px on page 2 and 488 px in the gallery render s9620-40dg-2-front.png - and this is the largest, which is why it is the one used. GATE 1: the image is exactly the chassis with no white margin, 649 x 130 px for the datasheet's 440 x 89 mm. Its aspect is 4.992 against a true 4.944, 1.0 % out, so it is orthographic and carries geometry; each axis is anchored to its own datasheet dimension, 1.4750 px/mm across and 1.4607 down. THE COST OF THE MISSING GUIDE IS RESOLUTION, and it is severe: one pixel is 0.68 mm, so a 2 mm lamp is three pixels and a printed legend is four pixels tall. Positions in this file are good to roughly half a millimetre and no better, and NOT ONE PRINTED LEGEND ON THE PANEL IS LEGIBLE at any magnification - see the silkscreen and port-numbering entries below and the gaps register. Where a house pattern would have read a HIG figure at 8.6 px/mm, this model read a marketing render at 1.47.
provenance.fru-parts: three components were built for this device because nothing in the library fitted, and each is named for the part number the datasheet's ordering list gives: ufispace/psu-102-ac (PSU-102-AISB-1, 1000 W AC, 52.9 x 39.7) and ufispace/psu-102-dc (PSU-102-DISB-1, 1000 W DC, same envelope), and ufispace/fan-40802825 (FAN-40802825-HD, 52.4 x 87.2). The existing ufispace/fan-402825 is FAN-402825-HD at 51.5 x 42.2 - a different part number and half the height - and was NOT reused despite the two faces being drawn in the same design language. Checked std/ and common/ first: std/sfp-ganged, std/qsfp-ganged, std/qsfp-dd, std/rj45, std/rj45-ganged, std/usb-a, std/sma, std/smb, std/c14-inlet, common/led-arrow-sm, common/led-dot and common/ground-symbol all fitted and are reused.
provenance.grounding: measured - a circled earth symbol at (9.1, 39.4) on the front panel between the two PSU legends, about 3.5 mm across, drawn with common/ground-symbol (6.0 mm, the nearest library part, so it is drawn larger than the print). It is a MARK AND NOT A LUG: no hardware is visible at it in either render, and common/ground-symbol is the silkscreen-only component. No grounding point is visible anywhere on the rear.
provenance.left-cluster: measured on the front render, with the isometric render used to identify what each item is. Left to right along the upper row: a six-segment status lamp column at x centre 79.3 mm (five green segments and a yellow one at the bottom, on an even 2.53 mm pitch from y 19.85 to 32.52) beside a white printed legend strip at x 81.4-86.8; the OOB management RJ45 at x 89.5-105.8, y 20.5-34.9, a single 16 x 14 jack with green link lamps in its lower corners; a two-high stacked jack pair in one bright shell at x 109.8-126.1, y 10.3-33.6, openings 12.9 mm wide on a 12.0 mm row pitch; and a second stacked block at x 131.5-147.8 holding an RJ45 over a blue USB 3.0 Type-A. Along the lower row: a large gold SMA at (82.4, 45.2) with a 9.5 mm bezel, and two smaller gold SMBs at (106.5, 44.8) and (128.1, 44.8) with 6.1 mm bezels. THE ASSIGNMENT OF ROLES TO THE FOUR RJ45-FAMILY JACKS IS AN INFERENCE, and a strong one: the datasheet lists exactly four (OOB, serial console, ToD, BITS), the isometric render prints 'ToD' above the stacked pair and 'BITS' below it, and the remaining pair - RJ45 over USB - is the console-plus-maintenance block. The three coax jacks likewise: the datasheet lists one GNSS SMA and two SMBs, the SMA is physically the larger connector and is leftmost, and for the two SMBs the isometric render's legends read 10MHZ then 1PPS left to right, which is also the datasheet's own list order and is corroborated by the printed ink itself - the first legend measures 12 px of ink and the second 9, and 10MHZ is one character longer than 1PPS.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9620-40DG end of life' - no announcement. The datasheet is dated 20260810V01 and the platform is a current Qumran3a design; none-announced is a checked state, not an absence.
provenance.panel-perforation: measured, and it is the second thing the QSFP-DD end of the panel was missing. The faceplate carries hexagonal EMI perforation in three places: a patch above EACH of the four QSFP-DD cages (dark runs at x 253.92-274.08 / 284.17-304.33 / 314.42-334.58 / 344.67-364.83 mm and y 5.5-22.9 in the 520 px render's own frame - exactly the cage width, one per cage and not one per pair), a thin band above each QSFP28 block and another between its two rows, and ONE CONTINUOUS BAND running below the whole QSFP-DD block and above the SFP56 blocks. That band starts at the left edge of SFP56 block 1 and ends about 92 % of the way across the three blocks - it stops short of the last SFP56 column rather than running to the end of the panel, which is why it is drawn as 240.66 -> 411.06 and not to 425.11. It is about 1.5 hex rows deep and is bottom-aligned with the QSFP28 mid patches at 47.9 mm. THE PATTERN TOKEN WAS WRONG ON EVERY ONE OF THESE AND THE ERROR WAS INVISIBLE. All ten patches were first declared `pattern: holes`, which render.py draws as circles filled '#3c4046' on a transparent ground. This chassis's panel measures '#373e44' in the rasterised front view, so the perforation was being drawn two counts darker than the metal it was cut into and could not be seen at any zoom - the declaration existed, lint was satisfied, and the face rendered blank. They are now `pattern: vent`, the hexagonal token the rear face already used, which is both the correct SHAPE (the isometric render resolves the holes as hexagons, not circles) and dark enough to read. ITS CELL IS COARSER THAN THE HARDWARE: render.py's vent hexes are 5.1 mm across on an 8.86 mm horizontal pitch, where the real perforation measures about 3.4 mm pitch - six hex columns across a cage where the drawing gives two. The character is right and the count is not, and no finer hex primitive exists to reach for.
provenance.port-grid: measured, AND THE STANDARDS ARE WHAT MAKE IT SAFE. The three SFP56 blocks each show five bright vertical posts in the render - the block's two ends and its three internal dividers - at x 355, 376, 397, 418, 439 px for block 1, i.e. a port boundary every 21.0 px = 14.24 mm. SFF-8433's ganged port pitch is 14.25. That agreement to a hundredth over four ports is the strongest single fact in this model: it says the render is dimensionally honest AND that std/sfp-ganged is the right part, so the ports are laid out on the standard's pitch anchored to the measured block origins 240.66 / 304.39 / 368.11 mm (block steps 63.73 and 63.72, even to within a fifth of a pixel). Row pitch is 15.00, the belly-to-belly figure std/sfp-ganged records from a TE ganged cage; measured here as 21.0 and 22.5 px on the two blocks that resolve it, which brackets 15.00 and cannot distinguish it from 15.2. The QSFP28 blocks are 1-wide x 2-high ganged cages, three across the upper band and three across the lower, block centres measured at 241.5 / 284.0 / 326.5 px = 163.74 / 192.55 / 221.37 mm, an even 28.81 mm step. Each block's drawn aperture measures about 18.3 x 8.7 mm; std/qsfp-ganged's registry opening is 18.5 x 9.58, and THE REGISTRY IS WHAT IS SEATED - which is why each block's silver shell in this file is 24.58 tall where the render draws 23.3. That 1.3 mm is the difference between the module envelope the render shades and the bezel opening the standard dimensions, not a measurement error, and it is recorded rather than tuned away. The four QSFP-DD cages measure centres 388.5 / 432.5 / 475.5 / 518.5 px; laid out on the even 43.33 px step that fits them, 263.40 / 292.78 / 322.16 / 351.54 mm. Drawn aperture 18.6 x 8.2 against std/qsfp-dd's 19.0 x 10.0, again the module face rather than the opening. PITCH WAS TAKEN FROM FEATURES THAT REPEAT ONCE PER PORT - the cage divider posts, the lamp groups in each block's centre band - never from the shaded module faces, which are narrower than the ports that own them.
provenance.port-leds: photo-measured, and it took the ISOMETRIC render to settle. In the flat front image the centre band of every block carries a regular pattern of small marks, and at 1.47 px/mm a lamp, an EMI perforation and a printed numeral are the same three pixels. The vendor's angle render s9620-40dg-1-angle.png resolves them and they are three different things: the QSFP28 blocks' centre band is a 2-row dot matrix of EMI perforation and carries NO lamps (a per-column dark-pixel count confirms it - a regular 8-across grid repeated on every block, which no indicator layout looks like); the SFP56 blocks' centre band carries a GREEN UP/DOWN ARROW PAIR per column, one arrow per port; and each QSFP28 block's lamps are the up/down arrows on the pale strip BELOW it, not in the band. So: 24 arrows in the SFP56 bands (measured as green pixel groups at every column centre, 12 groups 10-11 px wide, band centre y 93.5 px = 64.00 mm); 24 arrows on the six QSFP28 strips (block centre +/- 6.4 mm, strips at y 51-55 and 112-116 px); and 8 round green lamps under the QSFP-DD brackets, two per cage at +/- 5.9 mm from the cage centre, y 58 px = 39.7 mm - those eight are the clearest lamps on the panel, lit green in both renders. Drawn with common/led-arrow-sm (2.25 x 2.0, the only arrow that fits the measured 3.6 mm pair spacing - common/led-arrow at 3.6 wide would overlap its partner) and common/led-dot. NO STATES ARE CLAIMED for any of them: with no HIG there is no LED table, and colour vocabulary is not something a render can be read for.
provenance.port-numbering: NOT SOURCED, AND THIS IS THE LARGEST SINGLE GAP. Every port on this panel is numbered on the hardware: the SFP56 blocks print numerals on their teal strips, the QSFP28 blocks print a pair on the pale strip under each block, and each QSFP-DD cage carries a blue label bar above it with a numeral on it. All of them are three or four pixels tall in the only image that exists and none can be read at any magnification. There is no HIG and therefore no Port Overview table. So `rel-pos` here is POSITIONAL WITHIN EACH FAMILY - SFP56 0-23 left to right and upper-then-lower within a column, QSFP28 0-11 across the upper band then the lower, QSFP-DD 0-3 left to right - and it is NOT a claim about what the vendor prints. In particular the datasheet's own '40-port' phrasing suggests a single 0-39 range across all three families, which this file deliberately does not assert because nothing states where it starts. No numerals are printed on the drawing for the same reason.
provenance.power: datasheet Environmental / Power Supply: 'AC input: 100 to 240V, 12A', 'DC input: -40 to -72V, 30A', 'Typical power: 268 Watts (no transceiver)'. The scope is the vendor's own and is carried verbatim: the figure is TYPICAL, it is the box with no optics fitted, and no ambient is stated. NO MAXIMUM IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE - there is no installation guide to carry the fully-configured figure the way the S9321-64E's does - so power-max-w is absent rather than estimated, and power-envelope is `bare` because 'no transceiver' is exactly what that means. The two 1000 W ordering lines are the supplies' ratings and live on their own contracts; neither they nor the fans' draw (unpublished) may be added to 268.
provenance.psu-bays: measured - two supplies stacked at the LEFT END OF THE FRONT PANEL, which is the shape of this platform: PSUs draw in at the front (both ordering lines say 'intake air flow') and the five fans exhaust at the rear. Module plates at x 21-99 px, y 3-61 and 65-123, giving a 52.9 x 39.7 face on a 42.4 mm vertical pitch. Nothing in library/components/ fitted - the existing UfiSpace supplies are 33.3, 50.5, 68.0, 73.0, 73.2 and 73.5 mm wide - so ufispace/psu-102-ac and ufispace/psu-102-dc were built for it. The chassis silkscreen reads 'PSU 0' beside the upper bay and 'PSU 1' beside the lower, printed vertically; both are legible in the isometric render and neither is legible in the front one.
provenance.rear-layout: photo-measured on the vendor's rear render s9620-40dg-3-rear.png. GATE 1 PASSES WELL HERE: the chassis body spans x 20-499 and y 28-124 px, 480 x 97 px for 440 x 89 mm, giving 1.0909 px/mm across and 1.0899 down - the two axes agree to 0.1 %. It is still only one pixel per millimetre. Five full-height fan modules fill the left 62 % of the face and the rest is blank metal with one vent field at the right. Module seams at x 30, 88.5, 146.5, 203.5, 260.5 and 318 px - steps of 58.5 / 58 / 57 / 57 / 57.5, which is a +/- 0.7 px scatter about an even 57.6 px and is drawn as the even 52.80 mm pitch it plainly is, with the scatter recorded here rather than reproduced as five different gaps. First bay at 9.2 mm from the chassis edge; module face 52.4 x 87.2, i.e. all but a millimetre of the chassis height. Vent field at x 378.6-427.2, y 13.8-73.4. The fans are numbered by the chassis: each module's flange prints 'FAN <n' and the five read 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 left to right as seen from the rear. The middle three digits are legible at 10x; the outer two are inferred from the run, which is why index-origin is 0 and why the per-bay digit is filed as a gap rather than printed.
provenance.right-end-feature: photo-measured, AND IT IS NOT THE TRIANGLE THIS FILE USED TO PRINT. At the right-hand end of the panel, past the last SFP56 column, sits a printed legend line with a small ROUND RECESSED FEATURE below it: in s9620-40dg-2-front.png the pixels at x 485-491, y 62-69 read as a bright 7 px text row (peaks 146/147/124/147) above a compact annulus at (488, 66.5) - a bright rim at 194 and 248 with a darker core at 19 between them. The isometric render shows the same thing at x 618-626, y 98-106 and agrees: a wide bright row over a narrow bright blob. The earlier reading of a downward triangle came from that silhouette - a wide row tapering to a narrow one - and there is no triangle; the silkscreen path asserting one has been removed, because ink the device does not carry is the one thing silkscreen must never invent. Drawn as two decor rects, a 2.7 mm '#b0b5bb' disc with a 1.2 mm dark core, centred (425.1, 33.5). WHAT IT IS REMAINS UNKNOWN and stays a gap: the legend above it is four pixels of cap height and does not resolve, and the control for that is already established in front-image and silkscreen - not one legend on this panel resolves in the flat render, and the five that resolve in the isometric all sit nearer the lens and face the camera more squarely than this one does. A recessed round feature with a legend over it is conventionally a reset pinhole or an ESD jack; neither is written down anywhere and neither is claimed here.
provenance.sides-top-bottom: DELIBERATELY SIZE-ONLY, and this is the second thing the missing guide cost. The four remaining faces are dimensioned from the datasheet's 440 x 250 x 89 and carry no drawn content, because no orthographic view of any of them exists: the intake holds a front elevation, a rear elevation and one isometric from the front left. That isometric does show the top cover (a plain sheet with a few shallow stampings) and the left side (a field of small holes), but it is a perspective view of a 250 mm-deep box seen at about 30 degrees and nothing on it can be positioned along the depth axis to better than a centimetre - guessing a screw pattern from it would be inventing four faces. L45's size-only warnings and the level-2 capability ceiling are the honest record of that. AXIS CONVENTION, stated because it was checked rather than because anything asymmetric depends on it: on a top view y = 0 is the REAR, on a RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT and on a LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR; every one of these faces is empty, so no coordinate here can be at the wrong end of an axis, and the convention is written down so that whoever draws them later starts from the house rule rather than from a guess.
provenance.silkscreen: ONLY ONE LEGEND ON THIS PANEL WAS READ FROM THE ARTWORK: 'S9620-40DG', top left. Every other string in silkscreen[] below is the DATASHEET'S OWN NAME for the interface whose printed legend sits at that position. The ink is there and was measured - the extents of each legend's pixels are what fixed the marks' x positions and font sizes - but at four pixels of cap height the glyphs are a smear in the flat render and only marginally better in the isometric one, where 'ToD', 'BITS', 'GNSS ANT', '10MHZ' and '1PPS' are readable and the rest are not. So MGMT, CONSOLE and USB are transcriptions of function, not of print. This is the same choice the S9321-64E made for its LED legends and it is filed as a gap here for the same reason. The network pictogram under the OOB jack is drawn as a path rather than guessed at as a word, because its SHAPE is legible even where its meaning would have to be spelled.
provenance.sources: THIS DEVICE HAS A DATASHEET AND NOTHING ELSE, and the whole model should be read in that light. UfiSpace has not published a hardware installation guide for the S9620 family - the intake's own SOURCES.md carries it on a watch list beside the S9620-32E and S9620-54DC for exactly this reason - so there is no component table, no dimension drawing, no port-ID table, no LED table and no per-FRU wattage anywhere. What exists is: the two-page datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/telco-aggregation/s9620-40dg-datasheet.pdf, sha256 37a4789b...), and three vendor gallery renders staged as working/intake/ufispace/photos/s9620-40dg-{1-angle,2-front,3-rear}.png. A SECOND WARNING ABOUT THE DATASHEET: its spec text is set as OUTLINED GLYPHS, so pdftotext returns the headings and none of the values, and the docling conversion in converted/s9620-40dg-datasheet/doc.md has the same holes - it lists 'PHYSICAL', 'ASIC', 'Chassis' and so on with nothing after them. Every specification quoted below was read by rendering the PDF's own pages at 200-400 dpi and looking at them. Anyone re-checking this file by grepping the converted text will find an empty document and should not conclude the vendor published nothing.
provenance.status-leds: measured, unnamed. Six lamps in a vertical column at x 79.3, y 19.85 / 22.39 / 24.92 / 27.45 / 29.98 / 32.52 - the segments measure 2.16 to 2.6 px apart and are drawn on the even 2.53 mm pitch that fits them, with the drawing's scatter recorded here rather than copied. Five render green and the sixth, bottom, yellow. The white legend strip immediately to their right prints six names and not one of them is resolvable; with no HIG there is no front-panel LED table to fall back on, so the six placements carry positions, no names and no states. Naming them from a sibling platform's table would be inventing a citation.
provenance.unidentified-front-mark: SUPERSEDED BY right-end-feature ABOVE, and left standing so the correction is visible rather than tidied away. This paragraph read the mark as 'two or three characters above a triangular glyph ... with no hole and no hardware near it', and drew the triangle. Re- reading the same pixels one row at a time - rather than looking at an interpolated enlargement of them - showed a legend line above a small round recessed feature, and no triangle at all. The 'no hardware' half of the sentence was the more damaging of the two: it closed off a question the image can in fact answer.
